title: Grateful Dead Live at Kezar Stadium on 1973-05-26
lineage: Dat -> CD -> Samplitude Professional v9.02 -> FLAC
source: SBD -> Master Reel -> PCM -> Dat D

ai_review.summary: Crystal‑clear soundboard recording of the marathon Kezar show with smoking “They Love Each Other,” epic “Eyes of the World” and a stellar second‑set flow.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑patched 5/26/73 Kezar tape is an immaculate soundboard capture that lets every instrument breathe, from Jerry’s front‑and‑center guitar to the tight stereo separation of Bob and Jerry. Musically it’s a high‑energy three‑set marathon highlighted by “They Love Each Other,” “Eyes of the World,” “Truckin’ > The Other One” and a punchy second set, with only a few lukewarm moments such as “Tennessee Jed.”

ai_rating.rationale: Overwhelmingly enthusiastic reviews praise both the performance and the pristine soundboard source; only a handful of minor technical complaints keep the rating just shy of perfect.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Crisp, clean mix with superb stereo guitar separation and balanced levels; occasional low‑level buzzing noted by a few listeners but generally inaudible on typical playback.

standout_songs: China Cat Sunflower > I Know You Rider
show_quality.setlist_flow: Three‑set marathon with a tight, upbeat first set, an explosive second set that builds momentum, and a jam‑heavy third set that maintains high energy throughout.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Front‑and‑center guitar tone praised as perfect; his solos described as “smoking” and “all over” especially on ‘They Love Each Other’ and the jam sections.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass highlighted as “ultrabass wizardry,” with powerful bombs, standout solo in The Other One and driving presence on Eyes of the World.
band_member_comments.Bob: Guitar praised for clear stereo placement; noted as phenomenal guitarist by a reviewer, with strong rhythm work throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s piano/organ work described as solid, with moments of Rhodes brilliance; generally positive though one reviewer felt he was slightly buried in the mix at times.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill’s drumming called tight and energetic, providing a steady backbone for the long sets.
